page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor features a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is relatively strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2067.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.49 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 10% at 2086.47, and the Geekbench multi-core score is in the bottom 25% at 2547.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 13.13 GB/sec and 14.34 GB/sec respectively.

Given its hardware profile, the c7i-flex.large offers an entry-level compute option where single-threaded performance is prioritized over parallel processing or memory-intensive tasks. It is suitable for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and minor web serving tasks, but is poorly suited for database operations, software compilation, or large-scale multi-threaded workloads.
